references.text: Jair from Gilead had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts and controlled thirty towns—a similar description of a judge with many sons riding on donkeys
Ibzan had thirty sons and thirty daughters—the same pattern of judges having many children as a sign of wealth and power
Jair judged Israel for twenty-two years—a similar formula describing a judge's service and duration
Ibzan from Bethlehem judged Israel—the same literary structure for minor judges with information about family and term of service
Elon judged Israel for ten years—part of the same series of brief descriptions of judges and their terms of service
